articles.title: Verizon in Talks to Buy Fidium in $6 Billion Deal, FT Says

articles.summary: A pair of Chinese firms installed Nvidia Corp.’s powerful Blackwell semiconductors in a Shanghai data center linked to Alice Huang, the woman at the heart of a controversy surrounding the US chipmaker. The gear installed at the Yangtze River Delta Project included a GB300 NVL72 rack, among Nvidia’s most powerful products, according to a serial number specified in documents submitted to Chinese regulators in November. Shanghai Shuoyao offered the hardware as collateral to obtain a 96 million yuan ($14 million) loan from Shanghai Innovation Bank, according to filings from the lender that were reviewed by Bloomberg News. Bloomberg's Tom Keene and Paul Sweeney get details from Olivia Levieux, Markets Strategist with Bloomberg News (Source: Bloomberg)
articles.title: Nvidia Blackwell Chips Turn Up at China Site Tied to Alice Huang

articles.summary: Grand Theft Auto VI arrived after 13 years in development and it was made without using any generative AI according to Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick. It smashed all kinds of records. Gordon Bellamy, Director of Ethics at the USC School of Cinematic Arts, discusses what Rockstar’s blockbuster says about the value of human-made content in the AI era, why its extraordinary launch could reshape holiday spending across the gaming industry, and what smaller studios can learn from GTA VI’s success. (Source: Bloomberg)
articles.title: GTA VI’s Success Makes the Case for Human-Made Games
